input.quote: Notwithstanding any provision in this Agreement, M&I's total liability under this Agreement shall not exceed payments made to M&I by Customer under this Agreement during the three (3) months prior to the event.
input.rationale: M&I's indemnity at § 14.2(B) (p0220) is strong on scope: it covers third-party US patent/copyright/trademark infringement by the Services or M&I's software, third-party claims re M&I systems, breach of M&I's representations, protected-class law violations, harassment, injury/death and property or financial loss from M&I's acts or omissions, with an express duty to defend and full notice/control/cooperation procedures at § 14.3 (p0221). It fails the fallback on two material terms, however: (i) § 13.4 (p0207) caps M&I's total liability, "notwithstanding any provision in this Agreement", at only three months' payments — roughly 0.25x annual fees and far below the fallback super-cap of 3x annual fees, which functionally guts the IP indemnity; and (ii) there is no procure/modify/replace continuity remedy or fee refund if an infringement claim lands (no such language exists anywhere — searches for procure/modify/replace returned nothing). We therefore target the fallback and make only those two changes. The three permissive "may exclude" elements are met a fortiori: the indemnity is unqualified and takes no Customer-modification, combination or specification exclusions, which is better for us, and we do not propose adding them. Preferred-only gaps we are not pressing here (no affiliates, no general breach-of-law or data-breach limb, and Customer's mirror indemnity at § 14.2(A)/§ 6.6(B) being broader than Customer-provided content plus Customer's breach of law) are noted for information only.

ops.text: C. Infringement Remedies. If a claim described in clause (i) of Section 14.2(B) is made, M&I shall procure for Customer the right to continue using the affected Services or software, or modify or replace it so that it is non-infringing. If none of those remedies is available, M&I shall refund to Customer the fees paid for the affected Services or software.

ops.oldText: M&I's total liability under this Agreement shall not exceed payments made to M&I by Customer under this Agreement during the three (3) months prior to the event. No lawsuit or other action may be brought by either party hereto, or on any claim or controversy based upon or arising in any way out of this Agreement be brought, after one (1) year from the date on which the cause of action arose; provided, however, the foregoing limitation shall not apply to the collection of any amounts due under this Agreement.
ops.newText: M&I's total liability under this Agreement shall not exceed payments made to M&I by Customer under this Agreement during the three (3) months prior to the event, except that M&I's liability for its indemnification obligations under Section 14.2(B) shall not exceed three (3) times the annual fees paid to M&I by Customer under this Agreement. No lawsuit or other action may be brought by either party hereto, or on any claim or controversy based upon or arising in any way out of this Agreement be brought, after one (1) year from the date on which the cause of action arose; provided, however, the foregoing limitation shall not apply to the collection of any amounts due under this Agreement.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] M&I's indemnity is presently capped at three months' payments by § 13.4, well below our fallback super-cap of 3x annual fees, and there is no continuity remedy for an infringement claim. We have added procure/modify/replace with a fee refund if none is available, and set the § 14.2(B) indemnity cap at 3x annual fees; all other wording of § 13.4 is unchanged.
proposal.summary: Add infringement remedies (procure/modify/replace, else refund) and carve M&I's § 14.2(B) indemnity out of the 3-month liability cap with a 3x annual fees super-cap.
